page: Microsoft Azure EC16es_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine hosted on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is provisioned with 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical Intel Xeon cores running at a clock frequency of 4.2 GHz. Memory capacity totals 128 GB, establishing an allocation of 8 GB per vCPU. Hardware cache resources include 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 260 MB of shared L3 cache. The x86_64 CPU supports Advanced Matrix Extensions such as AMX-tile and AMX-int8, alongside AVX-512 vector instruction sets and hardware-assisted cryptography. The instance contains no integrated GPUs and zero local disk storage.

Performance benchmarks show top-quartile execution in single-threaded compute, reaching a Geekbench single-core score of 2037.0 and a text processing score of 2508.0. Multi-core performance aligns with median cloud instance benchmarks, registering 11996.0 in Geekbench multi-core, 14458.96 in multi-core stress-ng, and 24211.96 in the PassMark CPU test. Memory and data processing throughput remain within typical mid-tier ranges, evidenced by a PassMark memory rating of 2346.31 and an in-memory Redis throughput of 19.17 million SET operations per second.

The absence of onboard storage necessitates reliance on remote network-attached disks, which impacts disk I/O architectures and total deployment overhead. Because the instance balances high memory capacity with solid single-core frequency and matrix instructions, it provides resource density for workloads demanding high memory-to-core ratios. Primary suitable workloads include in-memory key-value databases, enterprise transactional systems, data analytics, and intermediate caching layers.
description: Microsoft Azure EC16es_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine driven by an Intel Xeon processor running at 4.2 GHz. Configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores and 128 GB of RAM, it maintains an 8 GB per vCPU allocation alongside 260 MB of L3 cache. The CPU features hardware support for AMX and AVX-512 extensions. In synthetic testing, the instance achieves upper-quartile single-core performance with a Geekbench single-core score of 2037.0, while multi-core metrics, including PassMark CPU (24211.96) and stress-ng multi-core (14458.96), fall within median bands. Memory performance is standard for this tier, delivering 19.17 million Redis SET operations per second. The instance includes no onboard storage or GPU hardware, requiring network volumes for persistent data. It is targeted at memory-intensive enterprise workloads, relational databases, and in-memory caches.
